title: Songbook and Summer
premise: Odile Galloway, who survived a house fire that killed her husband, runs the last bookshop in the coastal town of Merrow's End while raising her seven-year-old daughter alone. When the local library's anonymous pen-pal program pairs her with Bram Tuller—the harbor master whose negligence verdict she blames for the fire—both begin pouring truths into letters they'd never say aloud, unaware who holds the other's pages. As the season's last ferry approaches, taking Bram to a mainland job and Odile toward another safe, silent winter, the letters' identities are exposed at the worst possible moment. Odile must decide whether survival means staying invisible or letting someone stay after the last train leaves, choosing love against the duty of her grief.
about_author: I. M. Halloran is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who wrote love letters for illiterate sailors on a remote Atlantic island. They now live in a converted ferry terminal with a dog named Margin and an unreasonable collection of secondhand hymnals.

chapters.title: The Assignment Slip
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Three years after the fire, Odile runs the bookshop in careful, measured routines until the librarian's anonymous pen-pal program drops a slip into her register drawer. She almost throws it away; her daughter Nell signs them up instead. Emotional beat: the first crack in Odile's armor of small safe steps.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Bram Tuller's POV. Harbor master Bram, drowning in guilt and a resignation letter he can't send, receives his pen-pal's first letter and finds himself confessing things he's never written down. He answers honestly for the first time in years. Emotional beat: relief disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought In
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile and Bram clash publicly over the pier's crumbling loading dock, their animosity on full display—while both secretly rush home to write tender letters to their anonymous correspondents. Dramatic irony tightens. Emotional beat: the gap between who they are and who they're becoming.

chapters.title: Nell's Question
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Nell asks why they never talk about the fire, and Odile deflects into a letter describing a night she can't remember without flinching. Her pen-pal's reply—gentle, knowing—unsettles her with its familiarity. Emotional beat: memory pressing against the walls she's built.

chapters.title: The Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram learns the mainland job is confirmed; the last ferry leaves October first. He begins writing his pen-pal a letter he never intends to send, and takes a shift repairing the bookshop's storm-shutter instead of packing. Emotional beat: the first choice made for love rather than escape.

chapters.title: Half a Confession
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile writes her correspondent the truth about the fire—the candle, the wind, the verdict she's carried against Bram's inspection report. Bram, reading it at the harbor office, recognizes details only she could know. Emotional beat: dread and longing colliding.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. An early gale traps Odile and Nell in the bookshop overnight; Bram arrives to shore up the roof and they shelter together, almost tender, almost honest. He nearly confesses he is her pen-pal. Emotional beat: intimacy at close range, terror at closer range.

chapters.title: The Reveal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The librarian's end-of-program mixer unmasks every pen-pal pair. Odile learns her tender correspondent is the man she's blamed for three years; Bram watches her face collapse and cannot speak. She burns his letters that night. Emotional beat: the climax—love and blame occupying the same body.

chapters.title: Last Train, Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram boards the last train to the ferry terminal with his resignation in his pocket. At the platform, Nell appears alone with a letter Odile finally wrote—not forgiveness, but a question. Bram misses the ferry deliberately and walks back through the rain. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in certainty, traded for hope.

chapters.title: After the Last Page
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Spring. Bram's inspection report is reopened and amended; the verdict she needed isn't innocence but honesty. In the bookshop's back room, three mugs steam beside a stack of letters being bound into a book. Nell asks if he's staying. He is. Emotional beat: love chosen against duty, memory kept without letting it rule.
